messages:
support-ic: Hey team — customer acct redwood-inc hitting intermittent 401s and 500s on streaming /v1/generate, plus downstream JSON parse failures when we try to validate the structured output. They reported higher latency too. Repro steps below.

carla: Thanks — can you paste the minimal request you used?

support-ic: Yep. Sanitized request: ```POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"model\": \"rwd-open-7b\",
  \"mode\": \"json\",
  \"prompt\": \"Generate items as JSON array with fields id,name,price\"
}```

ben: Do we have logs for the 500? stack traces?

support-ic: Attaching trimmed logs (from customer side): 
```
2026-03-17T15:00:01Z client->api POST /v1/generate 200ms
2026-03-17T15:00:02Z api->client stream truncated: connection reset by peer
2026-03-17T15:00:02Z stream last chunk: \"[ { \"id\": 1, \"name\": \"Foo\", \"price\": 9.99, }\"
```

alice: Ah — trailing comma in the streamed payload then truncation. That explains parse errors. Where do the 401s fit in?

support-ic: 401s happen sporadically for same acct approx once per 500 calls, then clears. Customer uses short-lived tokens minted by their auth service.

carla: Could be a race where token refresh overlaps request and we return 401 from auth proxy. Also streaming truncation might be network or our server closing connection due to OOM or sudden model fallback.

eng-oncall: I looked at infra metrics — no OOMs on the node. There is an increased tail latency on that model at the time. I see a model fallback event to a cheaper variant for 3s then recovery — that can yield truncated streams if the runtime restarts the connection.

ben: Two-pronged: 1) immediate guidance for customer to reduce error impact (client-side fixes + retry pattern) 2) internal follow-up on fallback behavior and token race.

support-ic: For the customer, suggested quick fixes I proposed: 
- enforce idempotent token refresh: refresh before token expiry, add jitter
- local parsing resilience: use streaming-parse tolerant approach, then attempt repair
- add client-side exponential backoff on 5xx with jitter (500ms -> 1s -> 2s -> 4s max)

alice: For JSON repair chain share this snippet: 
```:attempt_parse = try(json.loads(stream_buffer))
if parse fails:
  1) re-ask prompt: \"I attempted to parse the last response and it failed. Please output ONLY a valid JSON array of items with fields id, name, price.\"
  2) self-heal attempt: run regex to remove trailing commas and strip partial tokens
  3) if still fails, fallback to asking for newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON)
```

support-ic: Can you add concrete regex we can give the customer?

carla: Sure — simple cleanup rules (client-side): 
- Remove trailing commas before a closing bracket: `s/,\s*(\]|})/\1/g`
- Strip unexpected non-JSON prefixes/suffixes: `^[^\{\[]+|[^\}\]]+$` (use cautiously)
- If streaming, append closing bracket when stream ends unexpectedly.

eng-oncall: Internal note: runtime should avoid hard model restarts on short fallback windows; I'll open a ticket to add a graceful drain + stream trailer that signals truncated outputs instead of abrupt close. That will help our repair heuristics.

ben: Billing note: customer mentioned spike in billed tokens during retries. billing-bot, any suggestions?

billing-bot: Recommend advising customer to set a client-side cap on retries for cost control, and we can offer a temporary credits review for this incident. Also check if retries are hitting different model variants with higher token counts.

support-ic: Customer follow-up I plan to send: include the sanitized logs, the regex heuristics, the re-ask prompt template, recommended backoff policy, and ask if they can try pinning the model variant for 24h to avoid fallback.

alice: Re-ask prompt template we can share: \"You previously returned malformed JSON. Please return the exact valid JSON array and nothing else. If you need to correct, try to repair the last JSON by removing trailing commas and ensuring all strings are quoted.\"

carla: Also provide short repro checklist for them: 
1) reproduce with curl and --no-buffer to see stream chunks
2) capture first 3 chunks and paste to support
3) run simple regex cleanup and attempt parse locally
4) if parse fails, call /v1/generate with the re-ask prompt appended and include original output in a `context` field

eng-oncall: I'll track the runtime ticket, assign to runtime-team, and add logs correlation for fallback events. Ben — can you own the on-call eng follow-up?

ben: I got it. I'll link the runtime ticket to this thread and ping runtime-team.

support-ic: Thanks all — I'll send the customer the steps in 10m and mark this as escalated to eng for the fallback behavior. :thumbsup:
